sections.content:
Getting a Saudi work visa as a Pakistani starts with employer sponsorship, not with the applicant. Your Saudi employer requests the visa through the Qiwa and MHRSD portals and secures a Visa Authorization, known as the Muqadam number. Without this authorization, no application can move forward.

Once the authorization exists, you complete the Enjaz application online, undergo a GAMCA or Wafid medical examination at an approved center, and provide biometrics at a Tasheer or Saudi visa service center in Pakistan. Passport stamping then takes about 5 to 10 business days, with the total timeline from job offer to stamped visa typically running 3 to 4 weeks.

sections.content:
Saudi Arabia has introduced a three-tier work permit system tied to monthly salary. The High-Skilled tier requires 15,000 SAR per month or more, the Skilled tier covers 7,000 to 14,999 SAR, and the Basic tier covers 3,000 to 6,999 SAR. Your tier influences your benefits, family sponsorship rights, and job mobility.

Real openings show what typical offers look like. An October 2026 Overseas Employment Corporation advertisement for HVAC and mechanical technicians listed salaries around 1,800 SAR for candidates aged 22 to 40. Always compare any offer against the official tier thresholds before accepting.

sections.content:
Pakistanis working in 23 designated technical fields must pass a Professional Verification exam to prove their skills match Saudi standards. This applies to many engineering, technician, and trade roles, so check whether your occupation is on the list before applying.

Just as important is choosing a legitimate recruiter. Only agencies holding a valid BEOE Overseas Employment Promoter licence may recruit for overseas jobs, and the Overseas Employment Corporation posts verified openings. Never pay large upfront fees to unlicensed agents, and verify every offer letter against the employer's Qiwa record.
